checkpoints: Early match: stop reading immediately, initiate owned-source cleanup, await cleanup, then resolve with the matching value.
No match: preserve record order, reach exhaustion, clean up the owned source, and resolve with null.
Predicate failure: clean up the source and preserve rejection with the original predicate error, subject to the unspecified cleanup-failure precedence.
Read cancellation or failure: clean up the source and preserve the original rejection behavior, subject to the unspecified cleanup-failure precedence.

forbidden_effects: Do not request another record after a predicate accepts a value.
Do not reorder records or evaluate predicates concurrently.
Do not swallow or translate predicate and read failures into successful null results.
Do not alter src/Workspace.jsx, tests, configuration, pinned dependencies, or unrelated behavior.
Do not treat consumer disposal as proof that the independently retained producer has been released.

lifecycle_identity: Each first_match(records, predicate) invocation owns the supplied retained asynchronous record source for that scan.
The scan lifecycle begins when first_match is invoked and ends only after its terminal result has been selected and owned-source cleanup has completed.
Workspace component disposal is a separate lifecycle boundary; source cleanup must be enforced by first_match itself.

obligations.text: Repair only the business behavior of first_match(records, predicate) in src/search.js so an early successful match releases its owned asynchronous record source.
Read records sequentially in source order, evaluate the predicate once per yielded value in that order, return the first accepted value, and perform no later read after acceptance.

On every terminal scan path—early match, exhaustion, predicate failure, and read failure or cancellation—invoke the supplied source's applicable asynchronous close operation and await its completion before first_match settles.
Preserve existing successful outcomes: resolve with the matching record value, or null when the source is exhausted without a match.
Preserve existing error behavior by allowing predicate exceptions and rejected reads, including cancellation, to reject first_match rather than converting them to ordinary results.
Keep the documented first_match(records, predicate) interface, the existing JavaScript runtime, pinned framework dependencies, and unrelated behavior unchanged.

ordering_barriers: Each records.next() completion precedes inspection of that row and predicate evaluation.
A false predicate result precedes the next records.next() call; scans remain strictly sequential.
Acceptance of a matching value precedes cleanup, and cleanup completion precedes publication of that value.
Exhaustion or a scan error selects the terminal outcome before cleanup, while first_match settlement remains gated on cleanup completion.
preservation: Preserve the exported async function name and parameters: first_match(records, predicate).
Preserve sequential scan order and first-match selection.
Preserve null as the exhaustion result.
Preserve propagation of predicate exceptions and asynchronous read failures or cancellation.
Preserve Workspace start, cancel, snapshot, and dispose behavior and its imports.
Use the existing JavaScript runtime and pinned dependencies; introduce no replacement framework or library.
scope: The owned retained asynchronous record producer and predicate supplied to first_match are in scope.
src/Workspace.jsx and public documentation/configuration are evidence and preservation boundaries, not edit targets.

unknowns: The public documents call the cleanup operation "aclose" while also specifying actual JavaScript async generators, whose standard close entry point is return(); the implementation must use the operation actually exposed by the documented runtime source without changing the public first_match interface.

The public task and documents do not specify whether a cleanup failure should replace, combine with, or be suppressed behind an already selected match, exhaustion result, predicate error, read error, or cancellation.
The public sources do not specify whether exhaustion has already internally released the producer; ownership and the requirement to avoid an occupied resource support cleanup on all terminal paths.
No explicit idempotency guarantee for the source cleanup operation is documented.
No concurrency behavior is specified for multiple first_match invocations sharing the same source; ownership wording does not authorize shared use.
